turns.speaker: Case manager
turns.text: Alright Terrell, recording's on. So you came home from Sheraton?

turns.speaker: Case manager
turns.text: And what day did you get out?

turns.speaker: Case manager
turns.text: Okay so you been home about a week?

turns.speaker: Client
turns.text: Yeah like eight days, it still feel weird.

turns.speaker: Client
turns.text: Fourteen. Forty, I said forty. Four oh.

turns.speaker: Case manager
turns.text: Lot of guys coming home need housing first, you good on that?

turns.speaker: Client
turns.text: Nah I'm good, I got my own place with my lady over in Chatham.

turns.speaker: Case manager
turns.text: Okay. And you're on MSR, who's your agent?

turns.speaker: Client
turns.text: Mr. Bell. I see him every other Wednesday.

turns.speaker: Case manager
turns.text: What do you need help with?

turns.speaker: Client
turns.text: Mainly a job. I did the culinary program inside, I want to cook. And my Social Security card, I don't have it.

turns.speaker: Case manager
turns.text: Okay, I'll print the SS-5 form for you today and we'll look at the culinary jobs Thursday.

key_info.comment: Client said May 3rd but also said he has been home about eight days, which points to November 3rd; confirm the date.
Case manager said MSR (mandatory supervised release), which is the closest choice to parole.

immediate_needs.detail: Wants a cooking job; did culinary program inside

next_steps.action: Print SS-5 form for Social Security card
